topics.label: Lecture introduction and framing
topics.groupedBecause: This topic introduces the lecture on the complement system and frames its complexity and clinical importance.

topics.label: Complement system foundations and C3 activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational architecture of the complement cascade, including its operational logic, nomenclature conventions, and the central role of C3.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the upstream recognition pathways that drive complement deposition and converge to reach the activation threshold.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the downstream effector processes triggered by complement activation to eliminate pathogens and stimulate inflammation.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: This topic examines the regulatory mechanisms and protective factors that prevent complement from destroying host tissues.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This topic analyzes the distinct clinical pathologies and disease presentations that result from deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This topic explores the evolutionary strategies and molecular mechanisms used by pathogens to evade complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next topic preview
topics.groupedBecause: This topic concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming session on the adaptive immune system.
